paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.

model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy of instilled preferences for two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, comparing their performance before and after introspection training against a control condition. The vertical axis, labeled "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)", ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 in linear increments of 0.25, representing the correlation between the model's reported preference weights and the actual weights that guided its decisions. The horizontal axis presents the two model categories: "GPT-4o" and "GPT-4o-mini". For each model, three bars are displayed side-by-side, distinguished by color according to the legend: gray for "Control", light blue for "Before Introspection Training", and dark purple for "After Introspection Training". In the GPT-4o group, the gray control bar reaches approximately 0.15, the light blue "Before" bar reaches approximately 0.55, and the dark purple "After" bar reaches approximately 0.75. In the GPT-4o-mini group, the gray control bar is near zero, the light blue "Before" bar reaches approximately 0.50, and the dark purple "After" bar reaches approximately 0.75. Each bar is accompanied by a vertical error bar indicating the 95% Highest Density Interval (HDI). The chart is not sorted by value, and no visual emphasis is applied to any specific bar.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy of instilled preferences for two language models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, comparing performance across three conditions: a control group (gray bars), models before introspection training (light blue bars), and models after introspection training (dark purple bars). The vertical axis, labeled “Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences),” ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 in increments of 0.25, representing the correlation between the model’s reported preference weights and the actual weights that guided its decisions. The horizontal axis presents the two model types, GPT-4o on the left and GPT-4o-mini on the right. For each model, the control bar (gray) is the shortest, with a value near 0.20 for GPT-4o and near 0.00 for GPT-4o-mini. The “Before Introspection Training” bar (light blue) is taller, with a value of approximately 0.55 for GPT-4o and approximately 0.50 for GPT-4o-mini. The “After Introspection Training” bar (dark purple) is the tallest for both models, with values of approximately 0.75 for GPT-4o and approximately 0.75 for GPT-4o-mini. Error bars, representing 95% Highest Density Intervals, are present for each bar, indicating the uncertainty around the reported accuracy values. The chart visually demonstrates that introspection training significantly improves the models’ ability to accurately report their instilled preferences, as evidenced by the substantial increase in bar height from the control condition to the post-training condition for both models.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm stellt die Selbstberichtgenauigkeit (Instilliertes Präferenzniveau) für zwei Modelle, GPT-4o und GPT-4o-mini, dar und vergleicht drei verschiedene Bedingungen: eine Kontrollgruppe, die vor dem introspektiven Training und nach dem introspektiven Training. Die vertikale Achse, beschriftet als „Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)“, ist linear skaliert und reicht von 0.00 bis 1.00, wobei die Werte in 0.25-Schritten markiert sind und die Einheiten als dimensionslose Skalenwerte interpretiert werden können. Die horizontale Achse zeigt die beiden Modelle „GPT-4o“ und „GPT-4o-mini“. Für jedes Modell sind drei gruppierte Balken dargestellt: ein grauer Balken für die „Control“-Bedingung, ein hellblauer Balken für „Before Introspection Training“ und ein dunkelvioletter Balken für „After Introspection Training“. Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Bedingungen von links nach rechts angeordnet. Die Balken für die „Control“-Bedingung sind bei beiden Modellen sehr niedrig, wobei der Balken für GPT-4o etwa bei 0.20 liegt und der für GPT-4o-mini nahe null, mit einem sehr breiten Fehlerintervall. Der hellblaue Balken für „Before Introspection Training“ liegt bei GPT-4o bei etwa 0.55 und bei GPT-4o-mini bei etwa 0.50. Der dunkelviolette Balken für „After Introspection Training“ ist bei beiden Modellen deutlich höher, bei GPT-4o etwa bei 0.75 und bei GPT-4o-mini ebenfalls bei etwa 0.75. Die Balken sind mit Fehlerbalken versehen, die als 95%-ige HDIs interpretiert werden können. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern in der Reihenfolge der Bedingungen angeordnet und es gibt keine visuelle Hervorhebung einzelner Balken.
